paras: The attempted lynching of French took place near Fort Logan, outside Denver, Colorado, late on a Friday night in mid-August 1903, when soldiers seized a Black man named French accused of assaulting a white woman and would have lynched him had the county sheriff not arrived. French survived, and the only known account, in a western Colorado weekly, gives no outcome.

According to The Delta Independent, a white woman identified as Miss Groom was visiting friends near Fort Logan and went down to Petersburg on an errand that Friday evening. Detained there, she missed the last car home and had begun to walk when French drove past in a wagon, said he was going to the fort, and offered her a ride, which she accepted. The paper described French as 'very light in complexion' and said he 'would readily be taken for a white man', while calling him 'a colored fiend'.

In the paper's account, French drove off the road and attempted an assault, choking the woman 'into insensibility'. Some soldiers rescued her and, the paper said, would have lynched French had it not been for the 'timely arrival' of Sheriff Gallaher, who had also heard her screams. The number of soldiers and what they did to French before the sheriff came are not stated.
The report does not say whether the sheriff arrested French, and no report of a charge, hearing or trial appears in the coverage found.

The episode survives in a single paragraph of a 'News of the Country Briefly Told in Short Paragraphs' column in The Delta Independent of 21 August 1903, set among items on a Jeffries–Corbett prize fight, radium arriving in Denver and the Russian fleet. The item stated the accusation as fact in the paper's own voice, opening with 'A lynching was narrowly averted near Denver' and naming the accused only as 'French'. It credited the sheriff with stopping the soldiers but offered no comment on their intent to lynch.
No Denver paper, wire dispatch or Black-press account of the episode was found.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of French near Fort Logan
bases: The only report says soldiers who came on the scene 'would have lynched' French and calls the episode a lynching 'narrowly averted', so it is an attempted lynching that killed no one (A1).

French was not killed: the report says a lynching was averted when the sheriff arrived; the would-be lynchers were 'some soldiers' of unstated number acting on an accusation of assault on a white woman (A1).
One paragraph in a Delta, Colorado weekly is the only report found in either press; no Denver paper, wire story or Black-press account turned up (A1).

accounts.label: Delta Independent news column
accounts.gist: French offered Miss Groom a ride, drove off the road and tried to assault her; soldiers rescued her and would have lynched him had Sheriff Gallaher not arrived.

framing.detail: A brief item in a news digest that treats the accusation as fact ('A colored fiend assaulted and choked into insensibility a white woman') and credits the sheriff's 'timely arrival' with averting the lynching, without comment on the soldiers.

record_check.dossier: 'near Fort Logan' / 'near Denver'; exact place not given
No county is named in the report
Inferred from 'late last Friday night' in a Friday 1903-08-21 issue; not printed
Black: called 'a colored fiend', though 'very light in complexion'
Threat/attempt to lynch; seizure is implied by the rescue but not stated

record_check.record: names the man French and the date as 'last Friday night'
record_check.dossier: Should also note the woman's name (Miss Groom), the sheriff (Gallaher) and that the man was described as 'colored'

info: 'Late last Friday night' in an issue dated Friday 21 August 1903, i.e. probably 14 August 1903; no calendar date is printed
Near Fort Logan, 'near Denver'; the woman had gone to Petersburg on an errand and was being driven back toward the fort
French (surname only), called 'a colored fiend' and described as 'very light in complexion'
Accused of assaulting and choking 'into insensibility' a white woman, Miss Groom, after offering her a ride in his wagon

sources.note: Paragraph in a 'News of the Country Briefly Told' column: soldiers near Fort Logan would have lynched French, accused of assaulting Miss Groom, but for Sheriff Gallaher's arrival; no outcome given.
quotes: A lynching was narrowly averted near Denver late last Friday night.
